The hosted kernel keeps its own way back in the GS base (SWITCH_TO_KERNEL_STACK is `mov rsp, gs:64`), so a guest gs_base written through zx_thread_write_state is not honoured: the test's save routine writes 0x7890abcd over the kernel's gs:0 and the kernel never comes back. Structural to libos.

Its first thread asserts zx_profile_create (unimplemented, NOT_SUPPORTED) and returns before locking the mutex or calling the second thread, which then waits on the channel forever; the guest never finishes and the suites after it (Timer, HandleWaitTest, Resource) are lost. Needs zx_profile_create / zx_thread_set_profile.

ApplyProfile: zx_profile_create is unimplemented and the test ASSERTs on it with a ZX_ASSERT (ud2 on x86_64, an UndefinedInstruction trap on riscv64), which kills the whole test process and with it every suite gtest had still to run. On riscv64 bare metal too: measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG) `ASSERT FAILED at profile.cc:74: status == ZX_OK` then `User mode exception: UndefinedInstruction` and `Exit status -1028`, and in CI it took the 50 requested cases of the suites behind it (952/1003) with it. x86_64 bare metal the same (`ud2`): measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG) at 310 s of the whole-suite boot, with 1032 cases passed before it and the 3 requested ones behind it never run.

SignalRequeue, INTERMITTENT (1 run in 6): after sync_completion_signal_requeue moved the waiters to the second futex, one of them was no longer reported BLOCKED_FUTEX (a spurious wake, or a state flip under the requeue), the test asserts and its destructor joins threads that nobody wakes. A real bug to chase; kept out so one bad run does not lose the suites gtest had still to run.

Resource.Ioports, the one case this prefix covers (a prefix because the platform's hang list rides in one guest option of at most 187 characters). It does port I/O after zx_ioports_request, and this kernel has no I/O permission bitmap: the request is a stub, and since user threads enter with IOPL 0 (as Linux and Zircon start them; IOPL 3 was the stand-in for the bitmap and made rflags unwritable through zx_thread_write_state) the `in` is a #GP that kills the whole test process. Measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG): `User mode exception: General` at 299 s of the whole-suite boot, `Exit status -1028`, with the 2 requested HandleWaitTest cases behind it never run. The table has it as FAILED; a real zx_ioports_request would be a TSS I/O bitmap switched with the process.

The suite drives what a hosted kernel cannot have: Ioports does outb(0x80) after zx_ioports_request, which is a #GP in a host process and kills the whole test process (exit -1028, every suite gtest had still to run lost); PcInterruptVectorPoolLeak never returns; the Mexec cases want a kernel to replace. Its three requested cases (ProbeAddressSpace, VmoCreation, VmoReplaceAsExecutable) go with it; the first two had skip entries already.

Address tagging (TBI) is not plumbed through the hosted aarch64 kernel: user pointers with a top byte are rejected (VmarTaggedAddress gets INVALID_ARGS from zx_vmo_create), the debug registers the segfault case reads back are NOT_SUPPORTED, and FutexWaitWake kills the whole test process (exit -1028: measured on the arm64 CI runner, #2516, run 42412571869, with the 375 requested cases behind it never run). Stripping the tag from user pointers on aarch64 is its own change.

Threads.WritingSingleStepState: zx_thread_write_state(ZX_THREAD_STATE_SINGLE_STEP) answers NOT_SUPPORTED on the hosted aarch64 kernel (single-stepping a guest needs MDSCR_EL1.SS and PSTATE.SS, which a host process cannot set), the test registers the fatal failure before ExitThread() and then waits on the suspended thread for ever: the whole-suite boot was cut at the 1200 s budget with 942 of 1051 requested cases passed and the suites behind it never run (arm64 CI runner, run 42415557086, after #2516). A prefix because the platform's hang list rides in one guest option of at most 187 characters.

PacketFollowsUnbindToWait and UntriggeredSignalInterruptWait, and only those two. Both need ZX_VIRTUAL_INTERRUPT_UNTRIGGERED (asserted while a virtual interrupt is idle, cleared from trigger to ack) and an unbind that hands the untaken packet's timestamp back to zx_interrupt_wait; here a zx_interrupt_wait that should return at once, or re-arm and block for the next trigger, never returns. Patterns, not names: the guest option is capped at 187 characters. On riscv64 bare metal too: measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG), an InterruptTest.* boot printed `[ RUN ] InterruptTest.PacketFollowsUnbindToWait` after 8 cases OK and nothing else until its 600 s budget, so the zx_interrupt_wait that never returns is the kernel's, not the host bridge's. x86_64 bare metal the same: measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG) the whole-suite boot printed `[ RUN ] InterruptTest.PacketFollowsUnbindToWait` with 1027 cases passed and nothing else until the 1200 s cut.

/RestrictedMode.*: restricted mode (zx_restricted_bind_state and friends) is unimplemented, and FloatingPointState, after its Initialize fails, never returns, so the run times out with every requested case already passed. Bare metal the same: the riscv64 CI boot on 13710b0 reached the suite at 1131 s (`syscall unimplemented: RESTRICTED_BIND_STATE`, `Initialize: failed to reset restricted state`) and printed nothing more until the 3600 s cut, 999/1003 in; the suite is the last one gtest runs, so nothing requested is behind it, only the exit.

Suspends a thread blocked in a syscall and writes rip=0 to it. Zircon interrupts the blocked syscall on suspend (INTERNAL_INTR_RETRY) and the resumed thread runs at rip 0 and dies; this kernel keeps the syscall blocked, so the written rip is never reached and the test waits for a termination that never comes. Bare metal x86_64 the same (the table has it as TIMEOUT): measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG) the whole-suite boot reached it at 211 s and sat on it until the 1200 s cut, with the 10 requested cases behind it never run (458/468).

PortStressTest.ChannelCallWaitQueuePanicRepro, the one case this prefix covers; a prefix because the platform's hang list rides in one guest option of at most 187 characters, and the names spelled out ran it to 204. Never finishes under QEMU TCG on riscv64: measured here (2026-11-07) still running after 700 s with the rest of the suite behind it, in a boot whose other 605 cases had taken 500 s. It is a stress repro of a wait-queue panic, not a correctness case; the three PortStressTest cases before it pass. Kept out so the suites after it are measured at all.

Kills the whole guest under QEMU TCG, so it has to stay out of the boot and not just out of the tally (needs_hardware only keeps a case out of the count; the positive filter is still `*`). TCG does not #GP on the non-canonical WRFSBASE, the write takes effect and the #GP arrives later on an FS-relative access with fsbase 0x1010101010101010 already in the saved context (trap_num 0xd, error_code 0x0, regs.rip 0x4000008ea34d, not the write instruction); the test then tries to put the thread back with zx_thread_write_state and the kernel refuses the non-canonical base (ZX_ERR_INVALID_ARGS, correct: it would #GP in ring 0 on the way out), the exception is left unhandled and the test process is killed with ZX_TASK_RETCODE_EXCEPTION_KILL (-1028), which lands on whichever [ RUN ] line is current: on master c665878 and #2506 b26d21d after Property.RegisterGsNoncanonical, on #2506 ddc5d7774 (Gs already out) after Property.RegisterFsNoncanonical itself. 173/468 every time, the 295 cases behind it never run. Needs real hardware, where WRFSBASE itself faults.

Same test body as Property.RegisterFsNoncanonical with GS (fsgsbase.cc, TestInThread), and the same kernel path refuses the non-canonical gsbase on write_state, so it kills the test process the same way; kept out of the boot with it. Measured in Test CI, Zircon Core Test Baremetal (x86_64): on master c665878 and #2506 b26d21d the -1028 landed right after '[ RUN ] Property.RegisterGsNoncanonical' (173/468); with this entry alone (#2506 ddc5d7774) the kill landed on the Fs case instead, which is why both are here. Needs real hardware.

Never finishes on riscv64: zx_thread_write_state answers ZX_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED for ZX_THREAD_STATE_FP_REGS and ZX_THREAD_STATE_VECTOR_REGS there (thread_state.rs implements those kinds for x86_64 only), threads.cc asserts ZX_OK on riscv (1275, 1297), and the RegisterWriteSetup destructor then resumes the suspended thread and waits for it to exit, which it never does. Measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG): the full boot stood 30 minutes in Threads.WritingFpRegisterState after 939 cases OK; Threads.* boots then hung the same way in Threads.WritingVectorRegisterState and Threads.WritingVectorRegisterStateUnsupportedFieldsIgnored, one per boot, and completed 8/8 with the three out. Two patterns rather than three names because the guest option that carries the hangers is capped at 187 characters; WritingF* and WritingV* match exactly these three in this image (the Reading* cases only fail, their ExitThread redirects the pc to zx_thread_exit). The FP and vector state kinds for riscv64, and why the resumed thread does not exit, are a tanda of their own.
See Threads.WritingF*: the same hang for the two vector-state cases, Threads.WritingVectorRegisterState and Threads.WritingVectorRegisterStateUnsupportedFieldsIgnored.

ChannelCallMutexTest.MutexHeldAcrossCallChain, the one case this prefix covers; a prefix because the platform's hang list rides in one guest option of at most 187 characters, and the names spelled out ran it to 204. Never finishes on riscv64: PROFILE_CREATE is an unimplemented syscall there (`syscall unimplemented: PROFILE_CREATE`), SetDeadlineProfile() fails with ZX_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED at channel_call_mutex.cc:60, and the case then sits until the boot's budget runs out. Measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG): the failure printed at 2781 s of the boot and nothing else until the 3600 s cut, with the 22 suites behind it never run. x86_64 bare metal the same (the libos entry is `ChannelCallMutex*`): measured here (2026-11-07, QEMU TCG) the whole-suite boot printed the `SetDeadlineProfile()` failure at 258 s and nothing else for the six minutes it was left, with 1015 cases passed before it.

Bti.NoDelayedUnpin, the one case this prefix covers; a prefix because the platform's hang list rides in one guest option of at most 187 characters, and the names spelled out ran it to 204. Passes on riscv64 but takes 1169 s under QEMU TCG (measured here 2026-11-07: `[ OK ] Bti.NoDelayedUnpin (1168935 ms)`, the next slowest case in the boot is 492 s), and with it the full boot does not fit in the hour it has: the run was cut at 3600 s with 22 suites still to go. Kept out of the boot so the rest is measured; it comes back the day the budget or the emulation allows it.

needs_hardware.reason: QEMU TCG does not #GP on the non-canonical WRFSBASE the test issues, so the write takes effect and the #GP arrives later on an FS-relative access: regs.rip is not the write instruction and the test's FATAL_PAGE_FAULT/cr2 assertions get General instead. Measured in the guest: both exceptions trap_num 0xd error_code 0x0, and the saved context already carries fsbase 0x1010101010101010 with no set_property in between. The kernel's own validation is correct and unit-tested (is_canonical_user_addr, zircon-syscall/src/object.rs). Needs real hardware.
